glosses: To be saturated with liquid by being immersed in it.

examples.text: I'm going to soak in the bath for a couple of hours.
Their land shall be soaked with blood.

glosses: To immerse in liquid to the point of saturation or thorough permeation.

examples.text: Soak the beans overnight before cooking.

glosses: To penetrate or permeate by saturation.

examples.text: The water soaked into my shoes and gave me wet feet.
The rivulet beneath […]soaked its way obscurely through wreaths of snow.

glosses: To allow (especially a liquid) to be absorbed; to take in, receive. (usually + up)

examples.text: A sponge soaks up water; the skin soaks in moisture.
I soaked up all the knowledge I could at university.
The case was that of a murder. It had an element of mystery about it, however, which was puzzling the authorities. A turban and loincloth soaked in blood had been found; also a staff.

glosses: To overcharge or swindle out of a large amount of money.

examples.text: It's a blackmail ring, and the district attorneys get a share of the loot. […] Well, they got him in the same kind of jam, and soaked him to the tune of three hundred and eighty-six thousand.
